_comment: The product's name, in one place. Everything a user reads comes from here:
the product name, the command, environment variables, the state directory,
the repository, the documents, the web UI.
Names written into a database or onto disk are deliberately NOT here. Those
are brand-free and frozen (schema bb, roles db_client/db_admin, pool dbpool,
containers pg-*, bucket wal-archive, key prefix key_, SQLSTATE BBX01/BBX02,
anchor format ledger-anchor/1), so renaming the product never touches an
existing install.
To rename the product: edit this file, run `make brand`, then
`bash scripts/rebrand.sh` for the prose and file names. See docs/branding.md.
tagline: the database that branches like code

_comment: The logo, in one place. `make brand` derives every size the app and the
README use from the four files in source/ — nothing is resized by hand,
and `make brand-check` fails if any derived file is stale.
To change the logo: replace the files in docs/brand/source/, set the
colours and the flags below to match, run `make brand`.
The sources carry their background baked in, as supplied. The generator
keys it out by distance from the corner pixel, so every derived asset is
transparent. Raise key_tolerance if new artwork leaves a fringe; raise
key_feather if its edges come out jagged.
wordmark_accent picks one letter of the product name out in the mark's
colours — the letter before the second capital, the x in FoxByte. The
logo that introduced it drew that x in a gradient; this one does not, so
it is off. The colours below are kept either way: they are the brand's
ink, and turning the accent back on should not mean finding them again.
touch_icon_plate is the ground behind the iOS icon, and is not optional:
iOS ignores a touch icon's alpha and composites it on black, so a
transparent one arrives as a dark smudge. The favicon has no plate.
